newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar climbs on thin supplies, little stock.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar climbs on thin supplies, little stock.

text.p: Sugar prices climbed further on the local market on Thursday, pushed by thin supplies and shortage of ready stock, despite slow demand from local consumers.

"Reports that the Indian government is considering a proposal to hike selling prices of sugar supplied through the public distribution system also prompted speculative buying in the open market," one broker said.
In the ready delivery sugar S-30 moved up by 12/15 rupees at 1,432/1,470 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 moved up by 10 rupees at 1,360/1,500 rupees per quintal.
"Higher outstation demand, particularly from the southern states, kept inflow of sugar low from the mills to the Bombay market," he added.

Most millers have already sold out about 80/85 percent of the free sale sugar quota of 800,000 tonnes released by the government for the current month. Market sentiment was firm at the end of the session.
